title: My Saviour, My Almighty Friend
description: My Saviour, My Almighty Friend in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 71, part 2, headed “Christ our strength and righteousness”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My Sa-viour, my al-might-y Friend, When I be-gin thy praise, Where will the grow-ing num-bers end, The num-bers of thy grace?

lines: Where will the growing numbers end,
And since I knew thy graces first
My feet shall travel all the length
And march with courage in thy strength
When I am fill'd with sore distress
How will my lips rejoice to tell
My soul redeem'd from sin and hell
My tongue shall all the day proclaim
His death has brought my foes to shame,
And drown'd them in his blood.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
